title: A skill hands the AI your procedure
caption: A skill can give an app a reusable procedure; how it becomes available depends on the platform.
request: Grab some mud here before we move on.

skill.gloss: Your proven procedure. An app can add it to context <marker>when the skill is invoked or activated.</marker>
skill.codeGloss: In Claude Code, SKILL.md instructions enter context when the skill is activated.

description.gloss: One line that describes when the skill may be useful.
description.codeGloss: The name and description at the top of the file.

project.gloss: What is specific to this project; when it loads depends on the app.
project.codeGloss: A project instructions file; Claude Code uses CLAUDE.md.

card.title: Collect sediment sample
card.description: Takes a sediment core. Use when we reach a new site and need a sample from the seabed.

steps.hold: Hold the robot 2 m above the seabed
steps.findFlat: Find a flat patch on camera
steps.core: Push the corer in, seal, lift

lines.samples: Samples go to the lab database

analogy: The pilot pulls one card from the dive manual when the dive needs it.

alt.closeUp: The research ship at the surface, its robot on a cable in the water, and a close-up of the control room on its bridge: the captain asks for a seabed sample, the pilot sits at the console, the project brief hangs on the wall, and one procedure card has slid out of the dive manual on the desk.

a-skill-spares-you-the-repeat.header: A skill spares you the repeat
a-skill-spares-you-the-repeat.description: Anthropic contrasts skills with prompts: a skill spares you from repeating the same guidance across conversations [1]. For Claude Code, Anthropic documents that SKILL.md content enters context on activation, such as through description matching or explicit invocation [1]. Other products may expose skills differently.

the-answer.title: The answer
the-answer.script: A useful idea is to write a procedure down once and keep it where the app can make it available for later tasks, instead of explaining it again and again. That is a skill, and in our picture it is a procedure card in the dive manual at the console. The rest of this Episode is about doing it well.

three-things-to-remember.title: Three things to remember
three-things-to-remember.script: Hold on to three terms, because we return to them all the way down. The skill is the procedure itself, the card. Its description is the one line that tells the model what the skill is for, an entry in the manual's index. And the project instructions hold what is true for this one project, the project brief on the wall.

the-card-slides-out.title: The card slides out
the-card-slides-out.script: And here is the part that matters most: a platform need not load every skill's full instructions at once. In a staged-loading pattern, it can expose descriptions and load a skill when invoked or activated, the way one card comes out of the manual for a dive. (pause) That is the picture for everything that follows.
